title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S/T a morphism of schemes (smooth in the intended application), E an O_S-module, and P^n_{S/T}(E) the sheaves of principal parts (jets) of E. Following the previous page, a stratification on E relative to T is encoded as a map δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E) with ε_E∘δ^∞_E = id_E. This is the 'second' (linear) structure, as opposed to the universal differential operator d^∞_E. Put d^+_E = d^∞_E − δ^∞_E. It lands in the augmentation ideal P^∞_{S/T}(E)^+ (formula (22)).

This page: compose d^+_E with the truncation P^∞(E)^+ → P^1(E)^+ ≅ E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}. This gives d^0_E : E → E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} (23), the connection attached to the descent ('recollement') datum. This is the classical passage from a stratification to its first-order part. If the datum satisfies the cocycle condition (is a stratification), the connection is integrable, so (23) extends to a de Rham complex E⊗Ω^•. Citing an earlier reference, he recalls the canonical maps (24) H^*_strat(S,E) := H^*((S/T)_strat, E_strat) → H^*_DR(S,E). These are functorial in E and compatible with base change.

He then announces the aim: an interpretation of H^1_strat(S,E) analogous to the earlier one for H^1_DR(S,E). That earlier interpretation (previous pages) is via affine torsors with integrable connection. The next page carries it out: a torsor under E_strat is the same as an E-torsor with a compatible stratification. This is computed via the exact sequence 0 → E → P^∞(E) → P^∞(E)/δE → 0.

A longer passage is crossed out. It introduces the cosimplicial sheaf C^n(E), the completion of E pulled back to the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal in (S/T)^{n+1}, with C^0 = E and C^1 = P^∞_{S/T}(E). The stratification makes C^•(E) a cosimplicial sheaf, more precisely a comodule over the cosimplicial ring C^•(O_S) (the Hopf algebroid of principal parts). The two cofaces C^0 → C^1 are δ^∞_E and d^∞_E. This is the standard Čech–Alexander / Hopf-algebroid complex computing stratified cohomology. He abandons this route in favour of the torsor description.
errors: Minor: equation labels are reused ((21) twice on the previous page; (24) used both for the comparison map and for C^0(E)=E, C^1(E)=P^∞).
'fonctoriels en F' is evidently a slip for 'en E'.

Implicit: the comparison map (24) is an isomorphism only under hypotheses (S/T smooth, characteristic 0). In positive characteristic it generally is not, since the stratifying site differs from de Rham there. The page does not claim an isomorphism, so this is not an error.

ideas.what: Stratification as a section δ^∞: E → P^∞(E) of the augmentation; its first-order truncation gives the connection, and the cocycle condition implies integrability.
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications vs. integrable connections (Hopf algebroid of principal parts)

ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968); EGA IV 16 for principal parts

ideas.what: Canonical map H^*_strat(S,E) → H^*_DR(S,E), functorial in E and compatible with base change.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial sheaf C^n(E) = completed jets on the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal of S^{n+1}, a comodule over C^•(O_S), with cofaces δ^∞ and d^∞ (crossed out).

deep.surprise_reason: A routine drafting page in the Gauss–Manin/Cartier material. It recalls the stratification-to-connection passage, the comparison map strat → DR, and starts (then crosses out) the standard cosimplicial jet complex. All of this is in Grothendieck's 1968 'Crystals' notes and in Berthelot's thesis.
transcription_corrections: 'Nous voulons une interprétation de H^*_strat(S,E) — analogue : elle donnerait [?] plus haut pour H^*_DR(S,E)' should read approximately 'Nous voulons une interprétation de H^1_strat(S,E) analogue à celle donnée plus haut pour H^1_DR(S,E)'. The superscripts are 1, not *, consistent with the torsor discussion on the next page.
'On sait alors [?] ] définir des homomorphismes canoniques' is more likely 'On sait [cf. [ ]] définir des homomorphismes canoniques'.
'fonctoriels en F' should be 'en E' (slip in the manuscript).

The crossed-out block starting 'Pour ceci, soit C^·(E) ...' extends through (25) and includes the line 'de faisceau cosimplicial [en fait, un comodule sur le faisceau cosimplicial C^·(O_S)]'. In (25), the left part shows a crossed-out first attempt 'δ^0_E, d^0_E : ... → P^∞_{S/T}(E)'.
